candidates.name: WebGL Fluid Simulation
candidates.description: Full-screen real-time Navier-Stokes fluid simulation that renders advected dye/smoke splats you can paint with the cursor. Implemented with raw WebGL using ping-ponged framebuffers, velocity/dye/divegence/pressure texture passes and optional multi-pass bloom.
candidates.creator: Pavel Dobryakov

licensing.notes: LICENSE fetched raw: 'MIT License, Copyright (c) 2017 Pavel Dobryakov'. Single-file (~2k lines) structure makes it easy to port.

candidates.research_notes: Demo served 200 and repository README verified. Source read 2026-11-03: script.js (51,849 bytes) — baseVertex shader plumbing, framebuffer/FBO ping-pong, linear-solve/advection/divergence passes and dat.GUI config panel all present; MIT header confirmed verbatim in-file.
candidates.otxyn_potential: High. Canonical fluid-sim reference; can be adapted for background liquid canvases, text reveal behind fluid, or cursor-painted liquid decoration.

candidates.name: WebGL Image Transitions slideshow (akella)
candidates.description: Codrops demo where a full-screen image slideshow transitions between images with GPU displacement-warp masks, giving a liquid-torn or smudge transition. Multiple demo variants (index files) show different warp/displacement strengths.
candidates.creator: akella (GitHub user 'akella', Codrops collab)

licensing.notes: Repo page fetched but license not checked.

candidates.research_notes: Demo URL fetched 200; repo discovered via search and confirmed by fetching its GitHub page. Classic displacement image-transition reference widely imitated in studio work.
candidates.otxyn_potential: High. Standard building block for image transition recipes; displacement-map technique ports to any WebGL stack.

candidates.name: WebGL Distortion Hover Effects
candidates.description: Hover a thumbnail and the next image is revealed through a displacement-map warp driven by a tweening WebGL shader. Uses a generated/photographed displacement image to morph one image into another.
candidates.creator: Robin Delaporte

licensing.notes: Codrops demo pages carry the Codrops demo usage terms; not read.

candidates.research_notes: Both the demo page and the tutorial article (titled 'WebGL Distortion Hover Effects'), verified by fetch. Article explains author and displacement-image technique explicitly.
candidates.otxyn_potential: High. The definitive 'displacement hover' recipe; small, portable, well documented in its tutorial.

candidates.name: WebGL Distortion Configurator
candidates.description: Interactive playground for building custom WebGL displacement hover/distortion effects over images: sliders/samples toggle RGB shift intensity, displacement strength and transition speed, with shareable URLs (index2/index4 variants).
candidates.creator: Anemolo (CodePen user; linked from article)

licensing.notes: Demo and article fetched; license not stated on fetched pages.

candidates.research_notes: Demo URL and tutorial article both fetched 200; article links author CodePen (codepen.io/Anemolo). Useful because it exposes the parameter space of displacement distortion effects systematically.
candidates.otxyn_potential: Medium-high. Good as a parameter-cheat-sheet for the library's displacement recipes rather than a standalone effect.

candidates.name: Audio-based Image Distortion Effects
candidates.description: WebGL image plane whose vertices/shading distort in response to audio (volume, frequency events), producing liquid warps that pulse with music. Six demo variants (index5 among them) show different intensity regimes.

licensing.notes: Demo + article fetched; license not stated.

candidates.research_notes: Both URLs fetched 200. Article title 'Audio-based Image Distortion Effects with WebGL' — the flow/audio-driven displacement pipeline is directly relevant to liquid motion recipes.
candidates.otxyn_potential: Medium-high. Shows how to map an external signal (audio) into liquid deformation — transferable to scroll/pointer/input-driven distortion.

candidates.name: Mouse Flowmap Deformation with OGL
candidates.description: Hovering drags a vector flowmap across an image, so background pixels smear like wet paint being pushed by a finger. WebGL velocity field is advected every frame and used as displacement input.
candidates.creator: Robin Delaporte

licensing.notes: Repo fetched for title only; license unchecked.

candidates.research_notes: Demo, tutorial article and repository all fetched 200. Flowmap is the cheapest convincing 'liquid smear under cursor' technique — no physics solver needed.
candidates.otxyn_potential: High. Compact, dependency-light (OGL) reference implementation of flowmap distortion. Strong library fit.

candidates.name: OGL official example: mouse-flowmap
candidates.description: Minimal example from the OGL library's example set that feeds pointer motion into a flowmap texture to shear/warp a textured plane. Shows the raw shader + uniform plumbing without any framework scaffolding.
candidates.creator: oframe (OGL author)

licensing.notes: OGL repository carries an open-source license (per repo page; exact text not fetched).

candidates.research_notes: Found in the OGL examples index (fetched, listed 'mouse-flowmap.html' among examples), demo verified 200. Complements liquid-006 as its framework-transparent counterpart.
candidates.otxyn_potential: High. Tiny dependency-free starter for flowmap effects; ideal as the library's 'learn from this' reference.

candidates.name: Liquid Distortion Effects (PixiJS + GSAP slideshow)
candidates.description: Image slideshow rendered with PixiJS where transitions apply liquid-like distortion filters tuned per-scene (a chrome/liquid look tuned per scene). GSAP drives the filter parameters between slides.
candidates.creator: Yannis Yannakopoulos

licensing.notes: Repository fetched — description reads 'A slideshow with liquid distortion effects in WebGL powered by PixiJS and GSAP'; license text not verified.

candidates.research_notes: Demo, tutorial article (author confirmed on page) and codrops GitHub repo all fetched 200. Notably shows PixiJS (2D sprite pipeline) rather than three.js — useful alternative stack for 2D liquid transitions.
candidates.otxyn_potential: High. Good PixiJS-based liquid transition pattern with explicit 'distortion as filter property' architecture.

candidates.name: Image Distortion Effects with SVG Filters (SVGImageHover)
candidates.description: Images and link thumbnails distort on hover using pure SVG filter primitives (feTurbulence-driven displacement maps), no WebGL involved. Multiple demo variants tune the filter channels for uglier/softer turbulence shapes.
candidates.creator: Manoela Ilic (Mary Lou)

licensing.notes: Demo and article fetched 200; license not stated.

candidates.research_notes: Demo, tutorial (author extracted from page) and Codrops hub listing all verified. The 'pure-SVG' class of liquid distortion — much lighter than WebGL for decorative hovers.
candidates.otxyn_potential: High. Perfect low-complexity counterpart for the library;SVG filters are widely supported and trivially embeddable.

candidates.name: Liquid Glass in the Browser: Refraction with CSS and SVG
candidates.description: Blog demo reproducing Apple-style liquid glass refraction on the web: edges of a glass panel physically bend background imagery using SVG displacement/refraction math layered under a frosted CSS backdrop-filter. Includes physics-derived lens-thickness displacement maps.
candidates.creator: kube.io (blog authors)
interaction: background glass-shaped distortion reacts to panel position

licensing.notes: Blog page fetched (353KB HTML incl. inline demo code); explicit license not stated.

candidates.research_notes: Found via keyword search, fetched 200. The page mixes instructional code and live demo in one page. This is the strongest 'glass distortion with physical refraction' recipe I found, aligned with 2025's liquid-glass trend.
candidates.otxyn_potential: High. The library needs a flagship glass/refraction entry and this covers the trendy Apple-liquid-glass aesthetic with standard web tech.

candidates.name: Creative Gooey Effects
candidates.description: Lucas Bebber's canonical SVG 'goo' filter: a heavy feGaussianBlur combined with an feColorMatrix alpha-contrast boost fuses separate DOM/SVG elements into metaball-like blobs that stretch and split, used for menus, buttons and droplets.
candidates.creator: Lucas Bebber

licensing.notes: Demo + article fetched; license not stated.

candidates.research_notes: Both URLs fetched 200; author extracted from article byline. The definitive goo/metaball filter demo (2015) that CSS-Tricks and countless CodePens derive from.
candidates.otxyn_potential: High. Must-have metaball recipe: ~30 lines of filter code, framework-free, huge visual payoff.

candidates.name: Canvas Liquid Effect (Matter.js + gooey filter)
candidates.description: Physics-simulated balls (Matter.js) merge into one liquid-looking blob because the canvas is post-processed through the SVG gooey filter (feGaussianBlur + feColorMatrix), producing a soft droplet that squashes and splits.
candidates.creator: n3r4zzurr0
techniques: SVG goo filter over canvas element

licensing.notes: Repo page fetched; license not verified.

candidates.research_notes: GitHub page (fetched) confirms approach: 'liquid (or gooey) effect on HTML Canvas using Matter.js and SVG Filters (feGaussianBlur and feColorMatrix)' plus a live demo link; demo page fetched 200.
candidates.otxyn_potential: Medium-high. Nearest 'DOM-friendly' liquid blob: 2D physics + filter pipeline is easy for agent templates.

candidates.name: Blobmixer
candidates.description: 3D blob-generation playground: users sculpt WebGL blobs through parameter panels (shape distortion, material, lighting, environment) producing psychadelic liquid-like 3D meshes with a debug-panel workflow.
candidates.creator: 14islands

licensing.notes: Site + case study fetched; source code not public as far as verified。

candidates.research_notes: Demo app and 14islands case study both deliver real content (fetched). Case study confirms stack: 'WebGL, Three.js, React JS, Next.js, Framer Motion' and describes the shape/material/lighting parameter system.
candidates.otxyn_potential: Medium. Inspirational benchmark for orchestrated parametric blob motion rather than a copy-able codebase; informs what 'controls' the library should expose.

candidates.name: Water Ripple FX with Canvas
candidates.description: Interactive 2D water-ripple simulator: two finite-difference wave-propagation buffers spread drop ripples from clicks/drag, with image refraction/shading applied per pixel so the background image bends like a pond.
candidates.creator: Almer ('Almeros' Coding Blog')

licensing.notes: Blog page fetched; code snippet appears in post but license unstated.

candidates.research_notes: Page fetched 200 with title 'Water ripple FX with Canvas and Javascript'. Reliable blog explaining the classic two-buffer ripple algorithm in plain JS + Canvas — no WebGL needed.
candidates.otxyn_potential: High. Pure-canvas ripple with transparent algorithm, ideal base for the library's ripple entries on a 2D budget.

candidates.name: WebGL Water
candidates.description: Interactive 3D water tank: heightfield water simulation with raytraced reflections and refractions, caustics, soft shadows, ambient occlusion and a draggable glass sphere; you draw on the water to create ripples.
candidates.creator: Evan Wallace

licensing.notes: LICENSE file at master/LICENSE returned 404 when fetched; license unverified.

candidates.research_notes: Demo page content confirmed via search-extraction (title/interaction list/features all present) and repository page fetched 200. The reference implementation for real refraction/caustics in the browser.
candidates.otxyn_potential: Medium. Mostly a teaching benchmark rather than an embeddable effect, but the caustics/refraction shaders are valuable extraction targets.

candidates.name: Glitch Slideshow
candidates.description: Image slideshow whose transition is a GLSL glitch shader: RGB channel separation, blockglic noise and displacement amount ramp in/out; demo 2 is the stronger chromatic-aberration variant.

licensing.notes: Codrops demo terms apply; not read.

candidates.research_notes: Demo 2 fetched 200 with title 'Glitch Slideshow | Demo 2 | Codrops'; located via Codrops hub search. Compact chromatic-aberration + glitch shader example suitable for study.
candidates.otxyn_potential: Medium-high. Best small chromatic aberration shader recipe found; easy to excerpt the RGB-shift pass into other transitions.

candidates.name: Wave Motion Effect on an Image with Three.js
candidates.description: A textured plane's vertices are displaced by rolling sine/noise wave functions in Three.js, so an image looks like it floats on water (wave swells, subtle shading). Multiple example scenes are linked in the article.
candidates.creator: Mario Carrillo

licensing.notes: Article fetched; embedded demo scenes not independently verified.

candidates.research_notes: Article (fetched 200; author extracted) contains full technique explanation plus linked demo files. The cleanest 'wave deform an image in 3D' tutorial found this session.
candidates.otxyn_potential: High. Small, teachable wave-deformation recipe that pairs well with displacement-hover entries in the library.

candidates.name: Interactive Droplet-like Metaballs (Three.js + GLSL)
candidates.description: GPU ray-marched metaball droplets that merge and split like liquid, with a simulated physics pass and mouse interaction; the tutorial covers the SDF-based metaball field with newly introduced GPU feature support.
candidates.creator: Yuki Kojima

licensing.notes: Repo fetched for title only ('Interactive metaball effect with ray marching, simu...'); license not verified.

candidates.research_notes: Article fetched 200 (author Yuki Kojima); its companion repo github.com/koji014/interactive-droplets fetched 200. Modern (2025) metaball approach — genuine ray-marched SDF field rather than the classic SVG goo trick.
candidates.otxyn_potential: High. State-of-the-art metaball technique; pairs low-tech SVG goo (liquid-011) with a GPU-accurate counterpart.
